subject.title: Session-store maintenance can evict an in-flight cron session entry mid run-prep -> every cron run fails with CronSessionLifecycleClaimError (and its 'Retry.' is never honored)

question: When protected durable entries already meet or exceed `session.maintenance.maxEntries`, should maintenance temporarily exceed the configured cap while emitting guidance, and where should the corresponding durable-pointer retention policy live?
rationale: Preventing destructive eviction is a clear safety requirement, but choosing a permanent over-cap warning and retention policy changes the documented operational meaning of `maxEntries`.

options.title: Protect entries and warn
options.body: Return without evicting removable sessions when the preserved population fills the budget, emit a bounded operator warning, and track durable-pointer retention separately.

options.title: Add durable-pointer retention now
options.body: Define and implement a safe retention policy for durable thread and channel pointers together with the non-destructive cap behavior.

options.title: Keep hard capping
options.body: Retain strict cap enforcement and require a different lifecycle-aware eviction design before changing the cap behavior.

recommendation.title: Protect entries and warn
recommendation.body: Return without evicting removable sessions when the preserved population fills the budget, emit a bounded operator warning, and track durable-pointer retention separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the active assignee and the decision spans session-maintenance product behavior rather than only the retry helper.
